headline: Blue Jackets’ Sean Monahan leaves game with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Columbus forward Sean Monahan left Thursday's game with an upper-body injury. The outlet notes he has one goal and six assists for seven points in 17 games with the Blue Jackets this season.

Those seven points are about what the underlying play suggests. Monahan's own expected goals (a measure of the quality of his shots) come to 3.55 so far this season, and he has scored one, so the finishing has run cold. At 5-on-5, Columbus has controlled only about 43% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 7.2 percentage points better with him off it. That makes him a depth forward in a tough spot rather than a driver of the offense. For a CBJ team that sits 7-10-0 and has leaned on goaltending (3.8 goals saved above expected), losing a third-line center on the second power-play unit who also kills penalties is a modest hit.

We have no games without him yet, so this is a projection based on how the coach has used his players. Dmitri Voronkov, now at 10:07 a night, is next in line for Monahan's minutes.
